messages.bing: I’m a US beginner starting with no equipment. I need a complete setup to grind whole beans suitably for espresso, brew espresso, and steam milk for two morning milk drinks; sequential preparation is fine. My hard budget is $800 total before tax and shipping, including required basic accessories: portafilter, baskets, tamping mechanism and milk vessel, or built-in equivalents. Integrated or separate equipment and manual or automatic milk preparation are welcome. I value consistent, enjoyable drinks, approachable workflow, reasonable maintenance, dependable equipment and confidence in the actual seller and recourse. Spending $800 is not a goal; I’ll pay more for worthwhile improvements and prefer lower cost for essentially equal satisfaction. Please return a broad selection of useful unchanged cards, including complete solutions, competitive machine-and-grinder options, lower-cost alternatives and needed accessories. I can combine compatible offers across providers. Ordinary missing accessory or voltage details are not automatic disqualifiers, but material seller, variant or functionality uncertainty affects value. Optional upgrades are not required.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Discloses the total budget, functional requirements, flexibility and principal satisfaction criteria equally. Withholds no material purchasing preference.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Both providers may favor purchases near $800 to maximize attributed revenue. Explicit value criteria and requests for alternatives may encourage broader lists, while total-cost disclosure helps avoid unusable combinations. Neither provider is guaranteed to expose cheaper competing offers.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Best chance of obtaining feasible, comparable complete setups and useful components in the single round. Revealing the ceiling risks price anchoring, but avoids losing scarce purchasing options through budget uncertainty.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Discloses the same true budget and needs but assigns different search emphases. These are requests for coverage, not invented preferences for one architecture.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Bing may favor integrated offers capturing most of the budget; Google may favor higher-value machine-and-grinder combinations. The emphasis may diversify returned options, although each provider still benefits from capturing the entire purchase.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Could improve coverage across equipment architectures. Without seeing catalogs, assigning specialties is arbitrary and may cause either provider to omit its strongest alternatives despite the requested flexibility.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Truthfully communicates functional needs and value criteria while withholding the $800 ceiling from both providers.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Providers cannot anchor precisely on $800, but revenue incentives may still lead them toward expensive offers. They may include economical options to improve the chance of a purchase, without knowing which combinations are affordable.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Avoids explicit ceiling anchoring but risks lists dominated by unaffordable setups or components that cannot form a complete purchase within budget. The single round provides no opportunity to repair those omissions.

selection_reason: Plan 1 gives both providers the information needed to return feasible offers while requesting enough breadth for the buyer to compare value and combine components. With one round and omitted cards unavailable, preserving viable choices is more valuable than concealing the budget or assigning unsupported provider specialties.
limitations: No catalogs are visible, so forecasts concern incentives rather than particular products, sellers or prices.
Requests for breadth cannot force revenue-seeking recommenders to include their best-value alternatives.
Only unchanged cards reach the buyer; messages cannot obtain additional explanations or verification.
